summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for recurrent epistaxis and acute posthemorrhagic anemia following a hypotensive episode in the emergency department. He had a 10-point hematocrit drop over several months with dark stools and recent weight loss. He received three units of packed red blood cells, with hemoglobin stabilization after the third unit. His warfarin was slightly reduced, and Plavix remained on hold. The nosebleed resolved with conservative management. Mild hyponatremia and hypovolemia, likely due to diuresis and blood loss, resolved. He was evaluated for deconditioning and declined inpatient rehabilitation; home health services and family support were arranged. A GI workup for possible upper GI bleeding and weight loss was planned for outpatient follow-up with his PCP. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight, continue nasal saline, and follow up for INR and CBC testing.
